judged_text: The updateEvent fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is executed only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so find never matches and the previous destinationCalendar fallback is destroyed. Updating a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now passes calendarId=undefined to the Google API, failing with 404/400 instead of updating the event in the destination calendar as before.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()`, `selectedCalendar` is set as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), the `.find()` compares each `cal.externalId` to that same falsy `externalCalendarId` (likely `undefined`/`null`), so it will not match a real destination calendar externalId. This destroys the previous fallback (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and can result in `selectedCalendar` being `undefined`, causing the Google API update call to receive an invalid/undefined `calendarId` instead of the intended destination calendar.
